Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106654; File No. SR-MIAX-2026-40]
October 13, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Exchange Act” or “Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on September 30, 2026, Miami International Securities Exchange, LLC (“MIAX” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the MIAX Options Exchange Fee Schedule (the “Fee Schedule”) to amend the Priority Customer Rebate Program (“PCRP”) table to modify the calculation used to determine the alternative rebates applicable to certain transactions in Complex Orders (all terms described below).
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://www.miaxglobal.com/​markets/​us-options/​miax-options/​rule-filings
,
and at the Exchange's principal office.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Section (1)(a)(iii) of the Fee Schedule to amend the PCRP table to modify the calculation used to determine the alternative rebates applicable to certain transactions in Complex Orders.
[
3
]
Background
Pursuant to the PCRP, the Exchange credits each Member
[
4
]
the per contract amount set forth in the PCRP table in Section (1)(a)(iii) of the Fee Schedule, as applicable, resulting from each Priority Customer
[
5
]
order transmitted by that Member which is executed electronically on the Exchange in all multiply-listed option classes (with certain exclusions described below), provided the Member meets certain percentage thresholds in a month as described in the PCRP table. The volume thresholds are calculated based on the percentage of national customer volume in multiply-listed options classes listed on MIAX entered and executed over the course of the month but does not include, in simple or complex as applicable, QCC
[
6
]
and cQCC Orders,
[
7
]
Priority Customer-to-Priority Customer Orders, C2C
[
8
]
and cC2C Orders,
[
9
]
PRIME
[
10
]
and cPRIME
[
11
]
AOC Responses, PRIME and cPRIME Contra-side Orders, PRIME and cPRIME Orders for which both the Agency and Contra-side Order are Priority Customers, and executions related to contracts that are routed to one or more exchanges in connection with the Options Order Protection and Locked/Crossed Market Plan referenced in MIAX Rule 1400 (referred to as “national customer volume”).
[
12
]
Pursuant to the PCRP, Priority Customer volume for transactions in simple, PRIME Agency, complex, and
(
printed page 65807)
cPRIME Agency are aggregated to determine the appropriate volume tier threshold applicable to each transaction. Volume is recorded for, and credits are delivered to, the Member that submits the order to the Exchange. All fees and rebates are per contract per leg. MIAX aggregates the contracts resulting from Priority Customer Orders
[
13
]
transmitted and executed electronically on MIAX from Members and Affiliates
[
14
]
for purposes of the thresholds described in the PCRP table.
Effective beginning September 1, 2026, the Exchange established alternative rebates for certain transactions in non-paired Complex Order volume based on a Member's Priority Customer total monthly non-paired Complex Order volume as a percent of the Member's Priority Customer total monthly volume aggregated to the PCRP.
[
15
]
Proposal
The Exchange proposes to amend the PCRP table to modify the calculation used to determine the alternative rebates applicable to certain transactions in non-paired Complex Orders.
Currently, the PCRP table provides the following volume thresholds applicable to Priority Customer Orders, which are based on a percentage of national customer volume in multiply-listed options classes listed on MIAX during the relevant month: 0.00% to 0.50% in tier 1; above 0.50% to 1.50% in tier 2; above 1.50% to 1.90% in tier 3; above 1.90% to 3.50% in tier 4; and above 3.50% in tier 5. Currently, for Priority Customer orders in the PCRP, the Exchange provides a per contract credit for non-paired Complex Orders based on a Member's Priority Customer total monthly non-paired Complex Order volume as a percent of the Member's Priority Customer total monthly volume aggregated to the PCRP. In particular, if the Member's Priority Customer non-paired Complex Orders account for less than 50% of the Member's Priority Customer total monthly PCRP volume, that Member's Priority Customer executed non-paired complex volume qualifies for the following rebates: (i) $0.20 per contract in tier 1; (ii) $0.21 per contract in tier 2; (iii) $0.26
[
16
]
or $0.27
[
17
]
per contract in tier 3 depending on whether the executing buyer and seller are the same Member or Affiliates; and (iv) $0.27
[
18
]
or $0.28
[
19
]
per contract in tiers 4 and 5 depending on whether the executing buyer and seller are not the same Member or Affiliates. If the Member's Priority Customer non-paired Complex Orders account for 50% or more of the Member's Priority Customer total monthly PCRP volume, that Member's Priority Customer executed non-paired complex volume qualifies for higher rebates as follows: (i) $0.23 per contract in tier 1; (ii) $0.27 per contract in tier 2; and (iii) $0.28 per contract in tiers 3, 4, or 5.
To calculate whether Members qualify for the alternative, higher rebates for their Priority Customer Complex Order volume, the Exchange compares the Member's monthly Priority Customer non-paired Complex Order volume to its total monthly Priority Customer volume aggregated for the PCRP. The aggregated PCRP volume includes simple, PRIME Agency, complex, and cPRIME Agency orders transmitted by that Priority Customer which are executed electronically on the Exchange in all multiply-listed option classes, with certain exclusions. The Exchange excludes the following orders from the calculation of Priority Customer Complex Order credits and from the calculation of the volume thresholds set forth in the PCRP table: QCC and cQCC Orders, Priority Customer-to-Priority Customer Orders, C2C and cC2C Orders, PRIME and cPRIME AOC Responses, PRIME and cPRIME Contra-side Orders, PRIME and cPRIME Orders for which both the Agency and Contra-side Order are Priority Customers, and executions related to contracts that are routed to one or more exchanges in connection with the Options Order Protection and Locked/Crossed Market Plan referenced in MIAX Rule 1400.
[
20
]
For purposes of calculating the Member's monthly Priority Customer non-paired Complex Order volume for the alternative PCRP rebates, the Exchange counts the volume of the option legs of a Complex Order and excludes the stock portion if the Complex Order is a stock-option order, as defined in Exchange Rule 518(a)(5).
The Exchange now proposes to amend the PCRP table to modify the calculation used to determine the alternative rebates applicable to certain transactions in non-paired Complex Orders. In particular, the Exchange proposes to include the Member's Priority Customer cPRIME Agency order volume in the calculation that currently compares the Member's monthly Priority Customer non-paired Complex Order volume to its total monthly Priority Customer volume aggregated for the PCRP. Specifically, the Exchange proposes to amend Section (1)(a)(iii) of the Fee Schedule to amend the last two column headings to insert the words “and cPRIME Agency” following the phrase “Per Contract Credit for Complex Orders, Priority Customer Non-Paired Complex Orders. . . .” With the proposed changes, the last two columns in the table in Section (1)(a)(iii) of the Fee Schedule will read as follows: “Per Contract Credit for Complex Orders, Priority Customer Non-Paired Complex Orders and cPRIME Agency Volume <50% of Member's PCRP Volume” and “Per Contract Credit for Complex Orders, Priority Customer Non-Paired Complex Orders and cPRIME Agency Volume ≥50% of Member's PCRP Volume”. Accordingly, to determine the alternative rebates applicable to certain transactions in Complex Orders for the
(
printed page 65808)
PCRP, the Exchange will compare the Member's monthly Priority Customer non-paired Complex Orders and cPRIME Agency order volume to its total monthly Priority Customer volume aggregated for the PCRP, which aggregated volume includes simple, PRIME Agency, complex, and cPRIME Agency orders transmitted by that Priority Customer that are executed electronically on the Exchange in all multiply-listed option classes. The Exchange will continue to exclude the following from the calculation of Priority Customer Complex Order credits and from the calculation of the volume thresholds set forth in the PCRP table: QCC and cQCC Orders, Priority Customer-to-Priority Customer Orders, C2C and cC2C Orders, PRIME and cPRIME AOC Responses, PRIME and cPRIME Contra-side Orders, PRIME and cPRIME Orders for which both the Agency and Contra-side Order are Priority Customers, and executions related to contracts that are routed to one or more exchanges in connection with the Options Order Protection and Locked/Crossed Market Plan referenced in MIAX Rule 1400.
[
21
]
The Exchange does not propose to amend any of the volume threshold percentages or credit amounts with this filing.
The purpose of this proposed change is for business and competitive reasons. With the proposed change to include Priority Customer cPRIME Agency order volume in the calculation used to determine the alternative rebates applicable to certain transactions in Complex Orders, Members may be able to more easily qualify for the higher PCRP rebates for their Complex Orders. The Exchange believes this may encourage market participants to submit more Priority Customer Complex Orders and therefore increase Priority Customer order flow, resulting in increased liquidity which benefits all Exchange participants by providing more trading opportunities and tighter spreads. The Exchange notes that at least one competing equity options exchange similarly provides for higher customer rebates based on the ratio of simple order volume to complex order volume, with certain segments and/or symbols excluded from the calculation.
[
22
]
Implementation
The proposed changes are effective beginning October 1, 2026.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal to amend its Fee Schedule is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act
[
23
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(4) of the Act
[
24
]
in particular, in that it is an equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members and issuers and other persons using its facilities. The Exchange also believes the proposal furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
25
]
in that it is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers and dealers.
The Commission has repeatedly expressed its preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”
[
26
]
There are currently 19 registered options exchanges competing for order flow.
[
27
]
Based on publicly-available information, and excluding index-based and singly-listed options, no single exchange had more than approximately 10-11% of the multiply-listed equity options market share for the month of August 2026.
[
28
]
Therefore, no exchange possesses significant pricing power. More specifically, the Exchange had a market share of approximately 10.22% of executed volume of multiply-listed equity options for the month of August 2026.
[
29
]
The Exchange believes its proposal to amend the PCRP to include Priority Customer cPRIME Agency order volume in the calculation used to determine the alternative rebates applicable to certain transactions in Complex Orders is reasonable, equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because Members may be able to more easily qualify for the higher PCRP rebates for their Complex Orders. The Exchange believes this change is reasonable because it may encourage market participants to submit more Priority Customer Complex Orders, both non-paired Complex Orders and cPRIME orders, and therefore increase Priority Customer order flow, resulting in increased liquidity which benefits all Exchange participants by providing more trading opportunities and tighter spreads. The Exchange believes the proposed change to the PCRP is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it will apply equally to all market participants who provide Priority Customer cPRIME Agency order volume. The Exchange believes the proposed change is reasonable because at least one competing equity options exchange similarly provides for higher customer rebates based on the ratio of simple order volume to complex order volume, with certain segments and/or symbols excluded from the calculation.
[
30
]
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange believes that the proposed change will not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
Intra-Market Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposal will impose any burden on intra-market competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Exchange believes its proposal to amend the PCRP to include cPRIME Agency order volume in the calculation used to determine the alternative rebates applicable to certain transactions in Complex Orders will not impose any burden on intra-market competition. Instead, the Exchange believes this
(
printed page 65809)
proposed change will promote competition because it would encourage market participants to submit more Priority Customer cPRIME Agency order volume and therefore increase Priority Customer order flow, resulting in increased liquidity which benefits all Exchange participants by providing more trading opportunities and tighter spreads.
Inter-Market Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed changes will impose any burden on inter-market competition and the Exchange notes that it operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily favor competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive, or rebate opportunities available at other venues to be more favorable. There are currently 19 registered options exchanges competing for order flow. Based on publicly-available information, and excluding index-based options, no single exchange had more than approximately 10-11% of the multiply-listed equity options market share for the month of August 2026.
[
31
]
Therefore, no exchange possesses significant pricing power. More specifically, the Exchange had a market share of approximately 10.22% of executed volume of multiply-listed equity options for the month of August 2026.
[
32
]
In such an environment, the Exchange must continually adjust its rebates and tiers to remain competitive with other options exchanges. Because competitors are free to modify their own fees and tiers in response, and because market participants may readily adjust their order routing practices, the Exchange believes that the degree to which fee changes in this market may impose any burden on competition is extremely limited. The Exchange believes that the proposed rule changes reflect this competitive environment because they modify the Exchange's rebates in a manner that encourages market participants to continue to provide liquidity and to send order flow to the Exchange. The Exchange notes that at least one competing equity options exchange similarly provides for higher customer rebates based on the ratio of simple order volume to complex order volume, with certain segments and/or symbols excluded from the calculation.
[
33
]
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act,
[
34
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(2)
[
35
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-MIAX-2026-40  on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-MIAX-2026-40. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-MIAX-2026-40 and should be submitted on or before November 6, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
36
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Long-Term Stock Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend the LTSE Fee Schedule To Add an Incentive Program for Market Makers
full_text:

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106653; File No. SR-LTSE-2026-22]
October 13, 2026.
Pursuant to the provisions of Section 19(b)(1) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on September 30, 2026, Long-Term Stock Exchange, Inc. (“LTSE” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II and III below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange is filing with the Commission a proposed rule change to amend the LTSE Fee Schedule to add an incentive program for Market Makers.
[
3
]
The Exchange proposes to implement the changes to the fee schedule pursuant to this proposal on October 1, 2026.
The text of the proposed rule change is available at the Exchange's website at
https://longtermstockexchange.com/​
,
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
(
printed page 65828)
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The self-regulatory organization has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
On September 29, 2026, LTSE amended its rules governing registered Market Makers.
[
4
]
Under LTSE's Market Maker rules, Market Makers receive no benefits for making markets. To attract Market Makers, the Exchange is adding to its Fee Schedule the Market Maker Incentive Program. This program is designed to improve market quality in many Non-LTSE-Primary- Listed Securities
[
5
]
that trade on the Exchange by incentivizing Market Makers to quote at the national best bid or offer (“NBBO”)
[
6
]
in Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Securities (defined below).
The Market Maker Incentive Program.
Under the program, a Market Maker that posts displayed quotes on the Exchange at the NBBO for the times specified below during the Regular Market Session (as defined in LTSE Rule 1.160kk)) in a Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Security, as defined below, in which the Market Maker is registered pursuant to Rule 11.153 will be eligible for the following monthly incentives, subject to the Monthly Incentive Cap (defined below):
Security type
NBBO obligation
Monthly incentive
Dually-listed securities
At least 70% @NBBO
$1,250
UTP Securities, excluding Dually-Listed (“Non-LTSE Listed Securities”)
At least 50% and less than 70% @NBBO
850
At least 70% @NBBO
1,000
A Market Maker's time at the NBBO is calculated daily and averaged across the month by aggregating the percentage of time during the Regular Market Session during which the Market Maker's Primary MPID (as defined in Rule 11.151(d)(12)) has at least one round lot displayed at the NBBO.
[
7
]
The Exchange excludes from its calculation of whether a Market Maker qualifies for the Market Maker Incentive: (1) any trading day that the Exchange's system experiences a disruption that lasts for more than 60 minutes during the Regular Market Session; (2) any day with a scheduled early market close; and (3) the “Russell Reconstitution Day” (typically the last Friday in June).
[
8
]
During the first month in which a Market Maker is eligible to participate in the Market Maker Incentive Program, for each security in which the Market Maker registers, it may earn a pro-rata share of the monthly incentive described above (calculated on a daily basis) if the Market Maker commences quoting in its registered security on a day after the first business day of the month. All of the other provisions apply during the first month, including the Monthly Incentive Cap and the Liquidity Incentive Program Exclusion (both defined below).
The Monthly Incentive Cap limits incentives for Non-LTSE Listed Securities in a billing month to no more than 20 for every one Dually-Listed Security in which the Market Maker is registered. The Monthly Incentive Cap constrains the amount of monthly incentives that the Exchange must pay and encourages Market Makers to register in Dually-Listed Securities in particular.
Additionally, where a Market Maker meets the quoting requirements for both the Market Maker Incentive Program and the Liquidity Incentive Program, the Market Maker Incentive Program incentive shall apply in lieu of the Liquidity Incentive Program incentive. This is referred to as the “Liquidity Incentive Program Exclusion.”
“Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Securities” are those securities that qualify for the incentives set forth in the Market Maker Incentive Program. The Exchange will maintain a list of Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Securities, which will be provided to Market Makers upon request, and that list will include all Dually-Listed Securities and certain Non-LTSE Listed Securities selected on the basis of their trading characteristics. Non-LTSE Listed Securities will be screened, applying several objective factors that relate to a security's trading characteristics, and securities that meet specific thresholds with respect to these factors will be included as Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Securities. These factors are share price, average daily volume traded, average daily notional value traded, intra-day volatility, and time at the NBBO,
[
9
]
and they are designed to identify securities in which increased quoting would be impactful to both LTSE and the market, but not unduly burdensome to Market Makers in meeting the quoting requirements to earn incentives under the program. LTSE will review the eligibility of Non-LTSE Listed Securities annually and update the list of Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Securities. The Exchange will provide Market Makers adequate advance notice of changes to the list (if any). The balance between the quoting thresholds and the incentives offered under the program are discussed below.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act
[
10
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4)
[
11
]
and 6(b)(5)
[
12
]
of the Act in particular.
(
printed page 65829)
(1) Section 6(b)(4) Analysis
Section 6(b)(4) of the Act requires that the rules of a national securities exchange provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among all of its Members and issuers and other persons using its facilities. With the addition of the Market Maker Incentive Program to its Fee Schedule, the Exchange's rules will continue to provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members and issuers and other persons using its facilities.
The amounts of the incentives are reasonable.
Under the proposed Market Maker Incentive Program, LTSE offers Marker Makers the opportunity to earn monthly payments of $850, $1,000, and $1,250 per Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Security (depending on time spent at the NBBO and whether the security is a Dually-Listed Security or a Non-LTSE Listed Security), subject to the Monthly Incentive Cap, which limits incentives for Non-LTSE Listed Securities in a billing month to no more than 20 for every Dually-Listed Security in which the Market Maker is registered. The Exchange believes these incentive levels are reasonable in the current environment where, as discussed below, competitive forces constrain the Exchange's fees and drive incentives. By way of comparison, the proposed incentives are comparable to those offered by NYSE American LLC.
[
13
]
A Market Maker may earn a pro-rata share of monthly incentives calculated daily, on a security by security basis, if the Market Maker commences quoting in one or more of its registered securities on a day after the first business day of the month, but this would apply only during the first month in which a Market Maker is eligible to participate in the Market Maker Incentive Program and would be subject to the other program provisions, including the Monthly Incentive Cap and the Liquidity Incentive Program Exclusion. Therefore, Market Makers would be compensated in direct proportion to the time they bear active quoting risks and obligations. Accordingly, the Exchange believes that the amounts of any pro-rata incentives would be reasonable for the same reason that the full incentive amounts are reasonable.
[
14
]
The Exchange operates in a highly fragmented and competitive market in which market making firms choose to make markets on venues based on fee and incentive levels. LTSE is only one of sixteen registered equities exchanges, all of which have rules permitting the registration of market makers. The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and also recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”
[
15
]
Accordingly, within this landscape, the Exchange believes that the amounts of its proposed incentives are reasonable.
With the addition of the Market Maker Incentive Program, the Exchange's dues, fees, and other charges continue to be equitably allocated.
The reward a Market Maker receives under this program is tied to achieving specific quoting thresholds:
a Market Maker must quote at the NBBO in a Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Dually-Listed Security at least 70% the time to earn $1,250; and
a Market Maker must quote at the NBBO in a Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Non-LTSE Listed Security at least 50% the time to earn $850;
a Market Maker must quote at the NBBO in a Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Non-LTSE Listed Security at least 70% of the time to earn $1,000.
The proposed reward levels are calibrated to levels of market risk taken on by a Market Maker and the projected benefits to the Exchange. Those projected benefits include increased liquidity available at the NBBO in Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Securities, improved price discovery generally and for Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Securities in particular, increased order flow to the Exchange, and improved trading conditions for all market participants on the Exchange through narrower bid-ask spreads.
[
16
]
Additionally, the proposed larger incentive for Market Makers in Dually-Listed Securities appropriately corresponds to the greater quoting requirement of 70% at the NBBO threshold. A Market Maker registered in a Dually-Listed Security that fails to reach the 70% threshold would not receive any incentive; in contrast, a Market Maker registered in a Non-LTSE Listed Security that quotes at the NBBO less than 70% but at least 50% of the time would still be eligible for an incentive. The proposed larger incentive for making a market in a Dually-Listed Security appropriately corresponds to the risk associated with the single quoting threshold, set at the higher 70% level. As described in greater detail below, the proposed larger incentive for making a market in a Dually-Listed Security also reflects the Exchange's: (1) proposed requirement to register in at least one Dually-Listed Security as a condition of earning any incentive under the program (by operation of the Monthly Incentive Cap), coupled with the fact that the number of Dually-Listed Securities are limited in number, which offers Market Makers limited choices in those securities; and (2) commitment to enhance liquidity in Dually-Listed Securities.
The proposed incentives would be subject to the Monthly Incentive Cap, which limits incentives for Non-LTSE Listed Securities in a billing month to no more than 20 for every one Dually-Listed Security in which the Market Maker registers. The purposes of the Monthly Incentive Cap are to constrain the amount of monthly incentives that the Exchange must pay and to incentivize quoting in Dually-Listed Securities. Market Makers must register in one or more Dually-Listed Securities to participate in the Market Maker Incentive Program. At this time, there are not very many Dually-Listed Securities and, as mentioned above, Dually-Listed Securities are automatically included as Market Maker
(
printed page 65830)
Incentive-Eligible Securities (
i.e.,
they are not subject to the objective criteria mentioned above).
[
17
]
The Exchange proposes to offer a higher incentive for quoting at the NBBO in Dually-Listed Securities to compensate for this lack of choice.
For these reasons, the LTSE believes that the addition of the Market Maker Incentive Program would result in a continued equitable allocation of Exchange revenues.
(2) Section 6(b)(5) Analysis
Section 6(b)(5) of the Act requires, among other things, that the rules of the Exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers or dealers. The Market Maker Incentive Program discriminates fairly among issuers, brokers, and dealers (and does not discriminate among customers) in ways that are standard among the national securities exchanges.
The Market Maker Incentive Program discriminates fairly among brokers and dealers. Only Market Makers that are registered in one or more Dually-Listed Securities are eligible to earn the proposed monthly incentives.
[
18
]
This type of discrimination is standard; national securities exchanges offer incentives and rebates exclusively to market makers. The criteria for becoming a registered Market Maker apply equally to all Members.
The Market Maker Incentive Program also discriminates among issuers in two ways, and both are fair. First, the Market Maker Incentive Program favors Dually-Listed Securities by automatically including Dually-Listed Securities as Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Securities. Its preference of Dually-Listed Securities (over Non-LTSE Listed Securities) is also reflected in the amount of the proposed incentives, which varies according to whether the Market Maker quotes in a Dually-Listed Security or a Non-LTSE Listed Security: for Dually-Listed Securities, Market Makers may earn $1,250 for quoting at the NBBO at least 70% of the time; for Non-LTSE Listed Securities, they may earn $1,000 for quoting at least 70% of the time, or $850 for quoting at least 50% of the time.
Enhancing liquidity in Dually-Listed Securities is a primary objective of the Market Maker Incentive Program, reflecting the Exchange's heightened commitment to issuers that have chosen to dual-list on LTSE. It is common for equity markets to preference market making in securities they list. Other national securities exchanges have adopted market making programs that apply
exclusively
to securities listed on the proposing exchange,
[
19
]
which is far more discriminatory than what LTSE proposes.
[
20
]
Additionally, while the amounts of the proposed incentives offered by the Exchange for quoting at the NBBO vary for Dually-Listed Securities and Non-LTSE Listed Securities, that discrimination is fair for the reasons discussed above (
i.e.,
the higher incentive offered for making markets in Dually-Listed Securities reflects Market Makers' lack of choice in selecting Dually-Listed Securities and the increased risk associated with the singular eligibility threshold).
Second, the Market Maker Incentive Program incentivizes market making in only Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Securities, and thus discriminates among issuers of Non-LTSE Listed Securities. The Commission has consistently permitted exchanges to adopt differentiated pricing (and rebates) for distinct categories of securities, provided that the distinctions are based on reasonable, non-arbitrary criteria and further the purposes of the Act. As discussed above, LTSE will include certain Non-LTSE Listed Securities as Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Securities by applying several objective factors that relate to a security's trading characteristics and designating the securities that meet certain thresholds with respect to these factors to be Market Maker Incentive-Eligible Securities.
[
21
]
The Exchange has permitted similar types of discrimination before,
[
22
]
and the discrimination in this proposal does not raise any novel regulatory issues under the Act.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange believes that the proposed change will not impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, consistent with Section 6(b)(8) of the Act.
[
23
]
To the contrary, the proposal is a competitive response to incentives offered by other exchanges.
[
24
]
The Exchange operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily choose to send their orders to other exchanges and off-exchange venues. Currently, the Exchange has less than 1% market share of executed volume of equities trading. In such an environment, the Exchange must continually adjust its fees and incentives to remain competitive with other exchanges and with off-exchange venues. Because competitors are free to modify their own fees and credits in response, and because market participants may readily adjust their order routing practices, the Exchange does not believe its proposed fee change can impose any burden on intermarket competition. The Exchange believes that the proposed change could promote competition between the Exchange and other execution venues, encouraging Market Makers to quote more competitively on the Exchange in a significant number of securities, promoting price discovery, and contributing to a deeper and more liquid market to the benefit of all market participants. In turn, this would encourage market participants to direct their orders to the Exchange.
With respect to intramarket competition, the proposed rule change is designed to attract additional orders to the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the proposed rewards would incentivize market participants to direct their orders to the Exchange. Greater overall order flow, trading opportunities, and pricing transparency benefit all market participants on the Exchange by enhancing market quality and continuing to encourage Members to send orders, thereby contributing towards a robust and well-balanced market ecosystem. Further, the Exchange notes that the Market Maker Incentive Program is open on equal terms to all Members who register as a Market Maker pursuant to Rule 11.150 and are registered in one or more Dually-Listed Securities. The proposed incentives are proportional and based on quoting at the NBBO, an objective measure; they are not discretionary grants.
(
printed page 65831)
For these reasons, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change will not impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.

The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106652; File No. SR-GEMX-2026-36]
October 13, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 1, 2026, Nasdaq GEMX, LLC (“GEMX” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the Market-Wide Speed Bump and the Kill Switch.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/​rulebook/​gemx/​rulefilings
,
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend the Market-Wide Speed Bump at Options 3, Section 15(a)(3)(B)(vii) and the Kill Switch at Options 3, Section 17 to eliminate the existing cross-market functionality between GEMX and its affiliate, Nasdaq ISE, LLC (“ISE”).
Background
The Market-Wide Speed Bump (“MWSB”) is a Market Maker risk protection under Options 3, Section 15(a)(3)(B)(vii). This protection provides Market Makers a market wide parameter by which the Exchange will automatically remove the Market Maker's quotes in all classes when, during a time period established by the Market Maker, the total number of quote removal events specified in Options 3, Section 15(a)(3)(B)(i)(a)-(d) and (B)(2) exceeds the market wide parameter provided by the Market Maker to the Exchange.
The Kill Switch, set forth in Options 3, Section 17, enables Members to initiate a message to the System to promptly cancel all existing orders and restrict entry of additional orders their FIX,
[
3
]
OTTO
[
4
]
and Precise
[
5
]
order entry protocols. Members may submit a Kill Switch request to the System for certain identifier(s) on a user level, and the System will send an automated message to the Member when a Kill Switch request has been processed by the Exchange's System.
Currently, the MWSB permits Market Makers to request the Exchange to set the market wide parameter for the MWSB to apply either to just GEMX or across both GEMX and ISE. Similarly, the Kill Switch currently permits Members to elect to have the Kill Switch cancel and restrict their order activity either on GEMX or across both GEMX and ISE. Where a Market Maker or Member elects to apply the protection across both markets, a breach of the market wide parameter under the MWSB, or a Kill Switch request, results in the corresponding action being taken on both GEMX and ISE.
Of the Nasdaq affiliated options exchanges,
[
6
]
only GEMX and ISE currently offer MWSB and Kill Switch functionality that may be applied on a cross-market basis; MRX
[
7
]
offers MWSB on a per-exchange basis only and MRX, Phlx, NTX Options, and NOM offer a Kill Switch protection on a per-exchange basis only.
Proposal
The Exchange has determined to harmonize the MWSB and Kill Switch functionality across the Nasdaq affiliated options exchanges, where applicable. Because the comparable protections, as applicable, on MRX, Phlx, NTX Options, and NOM operate on a per-exchange basis only, harmonization supports removing the cross-market functionality currently available between GEMX
[
8
]
and ISE.
[
9
]
The
(
printed page 65837)
Exchange accordingly proposes to amend the MWSB at Options 3, Section 15(a)(3)(B)(vii) to delete the sentence that presently permits Market Makers to request the Exchange to set the market wide parameter to apply across GEMX and ISE, and to amend the Kill Switch at Options 3, Section 17(a) and (a)(1) to delete the references that presently permit Members to elect cross-market application of the Kill Switch. Nasdaq ISE has filed a companion rule change to make conforming amendments to its MWSB and Kill Switch.
Following the proposed amendments, all Market Makers will apply MWSB parameters on a per-exchange basis on GEMX, and all Members will apply Kill Switch requests on a per-exchange basis on GEMX. ISE separately offers a MWSB rule at ISE Options 3, Section 15(a)(3)(B)(vii) and a Kill Switch rule at ISE Options 3, Section 17, in each case on a per-exchange basis. Market Makers and Members will retain the ability to configure separate risk parameters and to submit separate Kill Switch requests for each Nasdaq affiliated options exchange on which they are authorized to trade.
Implementation
The Exchange will announce the operative date of the proposed rule change in an Options Trader Alert. The Exchange will implement the change on or before Q2 2027.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
10
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
11
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section (6)(b)(5)
[
12
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes that harmonizing the MWSB and Kill Switch functionality across the Nasdaq affiliated options exchanges, as applicable, will remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system by promoting consistent, transparent, and predictable risk-management functionality for Market Makers and Members that access more than one Nasdaq affiliated options exchange. Today, Market Makers and Members that trade across the Nasdaq affiliated options exchanges must understand and administer two different models for these protections: (i) a per-exchange model on MRX for MWCB and Kill Switch and a per-exchange model on MRX, Phlx, NTX Options, and NOM for Kill Switch, and (ii) a hybrid model on GEMX and ISE that permits, but does not require, cross-market election for these two risk protections. The Exchange believes that this differential treatment is a source of operational complexity that does not correspond to any material difference in the underlying risk protection provided. Aligning GEMX with the per-exchange model reduces the risk of Market Maker or Member confusion or inadvertent misconfiguration when establishing MWSB parameters or submitting Kill Switch requests across markets.
The Exchange further believes that the proposed rule change will protect investors and the public interest by preserving the substantive risk protection provided by the MWSB and the Kill Switch on GEMX. All Market Makers will remain subject to the mandatory MWSB requirement on GEMX, and all Members will retain the ability to submit Kill Switch requests on GEMX. Market Makers will continue to have discretion to establish their own parameters, subject to Exchange-established minimum and maximum time periods and default values. Members will continue to be able to submit Kill Switch requests for certain Identifier(s) on a user level and will continue to receive an automated message from the System when a Kill Switch request has been processed. The only substantive change is that a Market Maker's MWSB parameters on GEMX will only apply to that Market Maker's activity on GEMX, and a Member's Kill Switch request submitted on GEMX only will apply to that Member's activity on GEMX, in each case without aggregation with activity on ISE. Market Makers and Members that wish to apply the corresponding protections to their activity on ISE will continue to do so pursuant to ISE Options 3, Section 15(a)(3)(B)(vii) (MWSB) and ISE Options 3, Section 17 (Kill Switch).
Removing these elections in the interest of harmonization is likewise consistent with the Act. Cross-market application of the MWSB and Kill Switch on GEMX and ISE is an available feature that Market Makers and Members elect (or decline) to use; withdrawing the election does not diminish the mandatory MWSB that applies to every GEMX Market Maker or the Kill Switch functionality that remains available to every GEMX Member.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intra-market competition because no Market Maker or Member will be disadvantaged relative to any other Market Maker or Member as a result of the proposed change. Further, Market Makers and Members that wish to obtain aggregated risk protection across multiple exchanges may continue to configure their own risk-management systems to that effect.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on inter-market competition. Rather, removing the cross-market election will bring GEMX into greater alignment with the risk-protection framework generally available in the U.S. listed options markets and will harmonize the Exchange's MWSB and Kill Switch with those of the other Nasdaq affiliated options exchanges, as applicable.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section
(
printed page 65838)
19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
13
]
and subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder.
[
14
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-GEMX-2026-36 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-GEMX-2026-36. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-GEMX-2026-36 and should be submitted on or before November 6, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
15
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

order entry protocols. Members may submit a Kill Switch request to the System for certain identifier(s) on a user level, and the System will send an automated message to the Member when a Kill Switch request has been processed by the Exchange's System.
Currently, the MWSB permits Market Makers to request the Exchange to set the market wide parameter for the MWSB to apply either to just ISE or across both ISE and GEMX. Similarly, the Kill Switch currently permits Members to elect to have the Kill Switch cancel and restrict their order activity either on ISE or across both ISE and GEMX. Where a Market Maker or Member elects to apply the protection across both markets, a breach of the market wide parameter under the MWSB, or a Kill Switch request, results in the corresponding action being taken on both ISE and GEMX.
Of the Nasdaq affiliated options exchanges,
[
6
]
only ISE and GEMX currently offer MWSB and Kill Switch functionality that may be applied on a cross-market basis; MRX
[
7
]
offers MWSB on a per-exchange basis only and MRX, Phlx, NTX Options, and NOM offer a Kill Switch protection on a per-exchange basis only.
Proposal
The Exchange has determined to harmonize the MWSB and Kill Switch functionality across the Nasdaq affiliated options exchanges, where applicable. Because the comparable protections, as applicable, on MRX, Phlx, NTX Options, and NOM operate on a per-exchange basis only, harmonization supports removing the cross-market functionality currently available between ISE
[
8
]
and GEMX.
[
9
]
The Exchange accordingly proposes to amend the MWSB at Options 3, Section 15(a)(3)(B)(vii) to delete the sentence that presently permits Market Makers to request the Exchange to set the market wide parameter to apply across ISE and GEMX, and to amend the Kill Switch at Options 3, Section 17(a) and (a)(1) to delete the references that presently permit Members to elect cross-market application of the Kill Switch. Nasdaq GEMX will file a companion rule change to make conforming amendments to its MWSB and Kill Switch.
Following the proposed amendments, all Market Makers will apply MWSB parameters on a per-exchange basis on ISE, and all Members will apply Kill Switch requests on a per-exchange basis on ISE. GEMX separately offers a MWSB rule at GEMX Options 3, Section 15(a)(3)(B)(vii) and a Kill Switch rule at GEMX Options 3, Section 17, in each case on a per-exchange basis. Market Makers and Members will retain the ability to configure separate risk parameters and to submit separate Kill Switch requests for each Nasdaq affiliated options exchange on which they are authorized to trade.
Implementation
The Exchange will announce the operative date of the proposed rule change in an Options Trader Alert. The Exchange will implement the change on or before Q2 2027.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
10
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
11
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section (6)(b)(5)
[
12
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes that harmonizing the MWSB and Kill Switch functionality across the Nasdaq affiliated options exchanges, as applicable, will remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system by promoting consistent, transparent, and predictable risk-management functionality for Market Makers and Members that access more than one Nasdaq affiliated options exchange. Today, Market Makers and Members that trade across the Nasdaq affiliated options exchanges must understand and administer two different models for these protections: (i) a per-exchange model on MRX for MWCB and Kill Switch and a per-exchange model on MRX, Phlx, NTX Options, and NOM for Kill Switch, and (ii) a hybrid model on ISE and GEMX that permits, but does not require, cross-market election for these two risk protections. The Exchange believes that this differential treatment is a source of operational complexity that does not correspond to any material difference in the underlying risk protection provided. Aligning ISE with the per-exchange model reduces the risk of Market Maker or Member confusion or inadvertent misconfiguration when establishing MWSB parameters or submitting Kill Switch requests across markets.
The Exchange further believes that the proposed rule change will protect investors and the public interest by
(
printed page 65833)
preserving the substantive risk protection provided by the MWSB and the Kill Switch on ISE. All Market Makers will remain subject to the mandatory MWSB requirement on ISE, and all Members will retain the ability to submit Kill Switch requests on ISE. Market Makers will continue to have discretion to establish their own parameters, subject to Exchange-established minimum and maximum time periods and default values. Members will continue to be able to submit Kill Switch requests for certain Identifier(s) on a user level and will continue to receive an automated message from the System when a Kill Switch request has been processed. The only substantive change is that a Market Maker's MWSB parameters on ISE will only apply to that Market Maker's activity on ISE, and a Member's Kill Switch request submitted on ISE will only apply to that Member's activity on ISE, in each case without aggregation with activity on GEMX. Market Makers and Members that wish to apply the corresponding protections to their activity on GEMX will continue to do so pursuant to GEMX Options 3, Section 15(a)(3)(B)(vii) (MWSB) and GEMX Options 3, Section 17 (Kill Switch).
Removing these elections in the interest of harmonization is likewise consistent with the Act. Cross-market application of the MWSB and Kill Switch on ISE and GEMX is an available feature that Market Makers and Members elect (or decline) to use; withdrawing the election does not diminish the mandatory MWSB that applies to every ISE Market Maker or the Kill Switch functionality that remains available to every ISE Member.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intra-market competition because no Market Maker or Member will be disadvantaged relative to any other Market Maker or Member as a result of the proposed change. Further, Market Makers and Members that wish to obtain aggregated risk protection across multiple exchanges may continue to configure their own risk-management systems to that effect.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on inter-market competition. Rather, removing the cross-market election will bring ISE into greater alignment with the risk-protection framework generally available in the U.S. listed options markets and will harmonize the Exchange's MWSB and Kill Switch with those of the other Nasdaq affiliated options exchanges, as applicable.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
13
]
and subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder.
[
14
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
. Please include file number SR-ISE-2026-54 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street, NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-ISE-2026-54. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-ISE-2026-54 and should be submitted on or before November 6, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
15
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.
