AGENCY:
U.S. International Trade Commission.
ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
Notice is hereby given that the U.S. International Trade Commission has determined not to review an initial determination (“ID”) (Order No. 8) of the presiding administrative law judge (“ALJ”) granting complainant GlobalFoundries U.S. Inc.'s motion to amend the complaint and notice of investigation (“NOI”) to assert dependent claims 8-12 and 19 of U.S. Patent No. 8,507,983 (“the '983 patent”).
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
B. Rashmi Borah, Esq., Office of the General Counsel, U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street SW, Washington, DC 20436, telephone (202) 205-2518. Copies of non-confidential documents filed in connection with this investigation may be viewed on the Commission's electronic docket (EDIS) at
https://edis.usitc.gov
.
For help accessing EDIS, please email
EDIS3Help@usitc.gov
.
General information concerning the Commission may also be obtained by accessing its internet server at
https://www.usitc.gov
.
Hearing-impaired persons are advised that information on this matter can be obtained by contacting the Commission's TDD terminal, telephone (202) 205-1810.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The Commission instituted this investigation
(
printed page 65776)
on April 30, 2026, based on a complaint filed by GlobalFoundries U.S. Inc. of Malta, New York (“Complainant”).
91 FR 23305-06
(Apr. 30, 2026). The complaint, as supplemented, alleges violations of section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended,
19 U.S.C. 1337
, based upon the importation into the United States, the sale for importation, and the sale within the United States after importation of certain semiconductor devices, products containing same, and components thereof by reason of the infringement of certain claims of the '983 patent and U.S. Patent Nos. 8,330,235; 9,093,425; 9,865,546; 10,062,748; and 10,707,167.
Id.
at 23305. The complaint further alleges that a domestic industry exists.
Id.
The NOI names eight respondents: (1) Tower Semiconductor Ltd. of Migdal Haemek, Israel; (2) Tower Partners Semiconductor Co., Ltd. of Toyama, Japan; (3) Tower Semiconductor Italy S.R.L. (Italy) of Milano, Italy; (4) Tower US Holdings, Inc. of Newport Beach, California; (5) Tower Semiconductor San Antonio, Inc., of San Antonio, Texas; (6) Tower NPB Holdings, Inc. of San Jose, California; (7) Tower Semiconductor Newport Beach, Inc. of Newport Beach, California; and (8) Newport Fab LLC of Newport Beach, California.
Id.
at 23306. The Office of Unfair Import Investigations is not named as a party to this investigation.
Id.
On August 31, 2026, Complainant moved to amend the complaint and NOI to assert dependent claims 8-12 and 19 of the '983 patent. Respondents did not oppose the motion.
On September 14, 2026, the presiding ALJ issued the subject ID (Order No. 8) granting pursuant to Commission Rule 210.14(b) (
19 CFR 210.14(b)
) Complainant's motion to amend the complaint and NOI. The ID finds that good cause exists for amending the complaint and NOI to add claims 8-12 and 19 of the '983 patent because Complainant obtained additional information during discovery that was not previously known to Complainant. The ID also finds that adding claims 8-12 and 19 of the '983 patent will not prejudice the public interest or the rights of any parties to the investigation.
No party filed a petition for review of the subject ID.
The Commission has determined not to review the subject ID. Accordingly, the complaint and NOI are amended to assert dependent claims 8-12 and 19 of the '983 patent.
The Commission vote for this determination took place on October 13, 2026.
The authority for the Commission's determination is contained in section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (
19 U.S.C. 1337
), and in Part 210 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (
19 CFR part 210
).
By order of the Commission.
Issued: October 13, 2026.
Lisa Barton,
Secretary to the Commission.

AGENCY:
National Park Service, Interior.
ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
In accordance with the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (NAGPRA), the Hudson Museum, University of Maine intends to repatriate a certain cultural item that meets the definition of an object of cultural patrimony and that has a cultural affiliation with the Indian Tribes or Native Hawaiian organizations in this notice.
DATES:
Repatriation of the cultural item in this notice may occur on or after November 16, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
Send additional, written requests for repatriation of the cultural item in this notice to A. Sky Heller, Hudson Museum, University of Maine, 5746 Collins Center for the Arts, Orono, ME 04469-5746, email
amber.sky.heller@maine.edu
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
This notice is published as part of the National Park Service's administrative responsibilities under NAGPRA. The determinations in this notice are the sole responsibility of the Hudson Museum, University of Maine, and additional information on the determinations in this notice, including the results of consultation, can be found in the summary or related records. The National Park Service is not responsible for the determinations in this notice.
Abstract of Information Available
A total of one cultural item has been requested for repatriation. The one object of cultural patrimony is a basket. The basket was collected from a cliff dwelling in Verde Valley, Arizona by an unknown individual at an unknown date and was among the collections of the Portland Society of Natural History located in Portland, Maine. The Maine Audubon Society, the successor organization of the Portland Society of Natural History, ceded the basket to the Hudson Museum, University of Maine in 1995. The Hudson Museum, University of Maine is not aware of the presence of any potentially hazardous substances used on the basket.
Determinations
The Hudson Museum, University of Maine has determined that:
The one object of cultural patrimony described in this notice has ongoing historical, traditional, or cultural importance central to the Native American group, including any constituent sub-group (such as a band, clan, lineage, ceremonial society, or other subdivision), according to the Native American traditional knowledge of an Indian Tribe or Native Hawaiian organization.
There is a connection between the cultural item described in this notice and the Yavapai-Apache Nation of the Camp Verde Indian Reservation, Arizona.
Requests for Repatriation
Additional, written requests for repatriation of the cultural item in this notice must be sent to the authorized representative identified in this notice under
ADDRESSES
. Requests for repatriation may be submitted by any lineal descendant, Indian Tribe, or Native Hawaiian organization not identified in this notice who shows, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the requestor is a lineal descendant or a culturally affiliated Indian Tribe or Native Hawaiian organization.
Repatriation of the cultural item in this notice to a requestor may occur on or after November 16, 2026. If competing requests for repatriation are received, the Hudson Museum, University of Maine must determine the most appropriate requestor prior to repatriation. Requests for joint repatriation of the cultural item are considered a single request and not competing requests. The Hudson Museum, University of Maine is responsible for sending a copy of this notice to the Indian Tribes and Native Hawaiian organizations identified in this notice and to any other consulting parties.
Authority:
Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act,
25 U.S.C. 3004
and the implementing regulations,
43 CFR 10.9
.
Dated: October 7, 2026.
Melanie O'Brien,
Manager, National NAGPRA Program.

Abstract of Information Available
The two associated funerary objects are a flint chisel and flint tool. These two objects were removed from the Goodall Mounds at an unknown date by Donald Boudeman. These two objects were donated to Michigan State University in 1961 by Donna Boudeman after Donald's passing. No known hazardous substances are present. These objects were part of a joint consultation effort to bring together human remains and associated funerary objects from multiple institutions together.
Cultural Affiliation
Based on the information available and the results of consultation, cultural affiliation is reasonably identified by the geographical location or acquisition history of the associated funerary objects described in this notice.
Determinations
Michigan State University has determined that:
The two objects described in this notice are reasonably believed to have been placed intentionally with or near individual human remains at the time of death or later as part of the death rite or ceremony.

In accordance with the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (NAGPRA), the Grand Rapids Public Museum (GRPM) has completed an inventory of human remains and associated funerary objects and has determined that there is a cultural affiliation between the human remains and associated funerary objects and Indian Tribes or Native Hawaiian organizations in this notice.
DATES:
Repatriation of the human remains and associated funerary objects in this notice may occur on or after November 16, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
Send written requests for repatriation of the human remains and associated funerary objects in this notice to Alex Forist, Chief Curator, Grand Rapids Public Museum, 272 Pearl Street NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504, email
aforist@grpm.org
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
This notice is published as part of the National Park Service's administrative responsibilities under NAGPRA. The determinations in this notice are the sole responsibility of the GRPM, and additional information on the determinations in this notice, including the results of consultation, can be found in its inventory or related records. The National Park Service is not responsible for the determinations in this notice.
Abstract of Information Available
Human remains representing, at least, 21 individuals have been identified (five of which are currently missing). Of the 174 associated funerary objects, 151 are present and 23 are missing. The 151 present objects are seven balls of earth, two bear jaw fragments, one bear tooth, eight bone awls and bone awl fragments, one bone pendant, two Busycon shell dippers, one canine skull, two cannel coal rubbing implements, one clay pipe, one core, one discoidal stone, one drill, two flint spades, two hammerstones, two lenticular stones, 13 lots of chips, three lots of galena crystals, one lot of mammal bone fragments, eight lots of mica, two mussel shell halves, two pieces of melted lead, two pipe casts, 33 pottery sherds, 26 projectile points, one red ochre paint stone, one sand conglomerate, 13 scrapers, five stone knives, one string of crinoidal sections, one tortoise carapace fragment, one ungrooved axe cast and four ungrooved stone axes. The 23 missing associated funerary objects are two balls of earth, two banded slate objects, one bone awl, one charcoal fragment, one copper awl, two drilled tablets, one earthen pot, one pendant, three pottery sherds, seven
(
printed page 65769)
projectile points, one scraper and one stone object.
The human remains and associated funerary objects were excavated by Elliott H. Crane (b. 1840-d. 1917) from Goodall Mounds (#12LE9), La Porte County, Indiana, at an unknown date. On July 10, 1917, the GRPM purchased a substantial number of objects from the Crane Estate. Crane was a collector and proprietor of Crane's Museum in Grand Rapids who excavated mounds in the Midwest in the late 1800s. GRPM continues to look for any missing human remains and associated funerary objects. No known hazardous substances are present. These human remains and associated funerary objects were part of a joint consultation effort to bring together human remains and associated funerary objects from multiple institutions.
Cultural Affiliation
Based on the information available and the results of consultation, cultural affiliation is reasonably identified by the geographical location or acquisition history of the human remains and associated funerary objects described in this notice.
Determinations
The GRPM has determined that:
The human remains described in this notice represent the remains of at least 21 individuals of Native American ancestry.
The 174 objects described in this notice are reasonably believed to have been placed intentionally with or near individual human remains at the time of death or later as part of the death rite or ceremony.
There is a connection between the human remains and associated funerary objects described in this notice and the Absentee-Shawnee Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma; Citizen Potawatomi Nation, Oklahoma; Forest County Potawatomi Community, Wisconsin; Kaw Nation, Oklahoma; Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas; Match-E-Be-Nash-She-Wish Band of Pottawatomi (previously listed as Match-E-Be-Nash-She-Wish Band of Pottawatomi Indians of Michigan); Miami Tribe of Oklahoma; Minnesota Chippewa Tribe, Minnesota (Mille Lacs Band); Nottawaseppi Huron Band of the Potawatomi, Michigan; Omaha Tribe of Nebraska; Pokagon Band of Potawatomi Indians, Michigan and Indiana; Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma; Ponca Tribe of Nebraska; Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation; Shawnee Tribe; Seneca Nation of Indians; and the Tonawanda Band of Seneca.
Requests for Repatriation
Written requests for repatriation of the human remains and associated funerary objects in this notice must be sent to the authorized representative identified in this notice under
ADDRESSES
. Requests for repatriation may be submitted by:
1. Any one or more of the Indian Tribes or Native Hawaiian organizations identified in this notice.
2. Any lineal descendant, Indian Tribe, or Native Hawaiian organization not identified in this notice who shows, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the requestor is a lineal descendant or an Indian Tribe or Native Hawaiian organization with cultural affiliation.
Repatriation of the human remains and associated funerary objects described in this notice to a requestor may occur on or after November 16, 2026. If competing requests for repatriation are received, the GRPM must determine the most appropriate requestor prior to repatriation. Requests for joint repatriation of the human remains and associated funerary objects are considered a single request and not competing requests. The GRPM is responsible for sending a copy of this notice to the Indian Tribes and Native Hawaiian organizations identified in this notice and any other consulting parties.

Abstract of Information Available
Human remains representing, at least, 191 individuals have been identified. The 484 associated funerary objects are projectile points, lithic tools, stone pipes, antler fragments, shark teeth, bone tools, marine and freshwater shells. These individual and associated funerary objects originated at a large mortuary site and precolonial campsite, spanning approximately 15 acres in Live Oak County, Texas. The site was used for mortuary treatment for approximately 300 years, although total site occupation extended from the Late Paleoindian period through the Late Prehistoric period. There were high densities of artifacts and over 400 cultural features including an isolated cache of lithic material dating to the Late Paleoindian or Early Archaic period. All materials and ancestral remains were first housed by the State Department of Highways and Public Transportation archaeology laboratory in Austin, TX after excavation. They were transferred in 1985 to CAR for long term housing. Sometime prior to their transfer, the ancestral remains were coated with Gelva, a clear-coated preservative.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
This notice is published as part of the National Park Service's administrative responsibilities under NAGPRA. The determinations in this notice are the sole responsibility of the SCHS, and additional information on the determinations in this notice, including the results of consultation, can be found in the summary or related records. The National Park Service is not responsible for the determinations in this notice.
Abstract of Information Available
A total of five cultural items have been requested for repatriation. The one unassociated funerary object is a doll with no head collected from Flaxman Island near Barrow, Alaska. The four objects of cultural patrimony are a wood tool with bone blade, bone tool with steel blade, piece of ivory with two drilled holes, and a horn ladle. All five items were reportedly collected by arctic explorer Ernest DeKoven Leffingwell, while he was stationed at Flaxman Island (1906—1914) and researching the region around Barrow, AK. These items were originally loaned to the SCHS in 1938 by Florence Van Orden and in 2025 were donated to the SCHS by her grandson Lucas Schuyler Van Orden IV. There is no known history of hazardous substances being used on these items.
Determinations
The SCHS has determined that:
The one unassociated funerary object described in this notice is reasonably believed to have been placed intentionally with or near human remains, and is connected, either at the time of death or later as part of the death rite or ceremony of a Native American
(
printed page 65762)
culture according to the Native American traditional knowledge of a lineal descendant, Indian Tribe, or Native Hawaiian organization. The unassociated funerary object has been identified by a preponderance of the evidence as related to human remains, specific individuals, or families, or removed from a specific burial site or burial area of an individual or individuals with cultural affiliation to an Indian Tribe or Native Hawaiian organization.
The four objects of cultural patrimony described in this notice have ongoing historical, traditional, or cultural importance central to the Native American group, including any constituent sub-group (such as a band, clan, lineage, ceremonial society, or other subdivision), according to the Native American traditional knowledge of an Indian Tribe or Native Hawaiian organization.
There is a connection between the cultural items described in this notice and the Native Village of Barrow Inupiat Traditional Government.

. Repatriation of the cultural items in this notice to a requestor may occur on or after November 16, 2026. If competing requests for repatriation are received, the SCHS must determine the most appropriate requestor prior to repatriation. Requests for joint repatriation of the cultural items are considered a single request and not competing requests. The SCHS is responsible for sending a copy of this notice to the Indian Tribes and Native Hawaiian organizations identified in this notice and to any other consulting parties.

A total of two cultural items have been requested for repatriation. The two sacred objects are a red catlinite pipe bowl (PM# NA3942A) and a wooden pipe stem (PM# NA3942B) (hereafter referred to as “the pipe”). The pipe is associated with Chief Black Coal (c. 1839-1893), an important Northern Arapaho leader and pipe keeper. The pipe was given to U.S. Army Lieutenant Patrick Henry Ray (1842-1911) following an unidentified council meeting in approximately 1886-1887. AGENCY:
National Park Service, Interior.
ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
In accordance with the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (NAGPRA), the Fowler Museum at University of California Los Angeles (Fowler Museum at UCLA) intends to repatriate certain cultural items that meet the definition of objects of cultural patrimony and that have a cultural affiliation with the Indian Tribes or Native Hawaiian organizations in this notice.
DATES:
Repatriation of the cultural items in this notice may occur on or after November 16, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
Send additional, written requests for repatriation of the cultural
(
printed page 65766)
items in this notice to Allison Fischer-Olson, Fowler Museum at UCLA, Box 951549, Los Angeles, CA 90095-1549, email
afischerolson@arts.ucla.edu
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
This notice is published as part of the National Park Service's administrative responsibilities under NAGPRA. The determinations in this notice are the sole responsibility of the Fowler Museum at UCLA, and additional information on the determinations in this notice, including the results of consultation, can be found in the summary or related records. The National Park Service is not responsible for the determinations in this notice.
Abstract of Information Available
A total of 13 lots of cultural items have been requested for repatriation. The 13 lots of objects of cultural patrimony are ceramic sherds, faunal bone fragments, china fragments, and projectile point fragments. These cultural items were removed from the surface of CA-RIV-129, located in Riverside County, CA, in Spring 1953 by Dr. Clement W. Meighan. They were received by the Fowler Museum at UCLA in Spring 1953 and comprise Accession 63. Treatment history of these items is unknown. During consultations, these cultural items were identified as being affiliated with the Cahuilla Band of Indians.
Determinations
The Fowler Museum at UCLA has determined that:
The 13 lots of objects of cultural patrimony described in this notice have ongoing historical, traditional, or cultural importance central to the Native American group, including any constituent sub-group (such as a band, clan, lineage, ceremonial society, or other subdivision), according to the Native American traditional knowledge of an Indian Tribe or Native Hawaiian organization.
There is a connection between the cultural items described in this notice and the Cahuilla Band of Indians.
Requests for Repatriation
Additional, written requests for repatriation of the cultural items in this notice must be sent to the authorized representative identified in this notice under
ADDRESSES
. Requests for repatriation may be submitted by any lineal descendant, Indian Tribe, or Native Hawaiian organization not identified in this notice who shows, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the requestor is a lineal descendant or a culturally affiliated Indian Tribe or Native Hawaiian organization.
Repatriation of the cultural items in this notice to a requestor may occur on or after November 16, 2026. If competing requests for repatriation are received, the Fowler Museum at UCLA must determine the most appropriate requestor prior to repatriation. Requests for joint repatriation of the cultural items are considered a single request and not competing requests. The Fowler Museum at UCLA is responsible for sending a copy of this notice to the Indian Tribes and Native Hawaiian organizations identified in this notice and to any other consulting parties.
Authority:
Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act,
25 U.S.C. 3004
and the implementing regulations,
43 CFR 10.9
.

AGENCY:

ACTION:
Notice of appointments to Performance Review Boards (PRBs).
SUMMARY:
Pursuant to
5 U.S.C. 4314(c)(4)
, this notice announces the appointment of members to the Department of the Treasury's Performance Review Boards (PRBs). The purpose of these Boards are to review and make recommendations concerning proposed performance appraisals, ratings, bonuses and other appropriate personnel actions for incumbents of SES positions in the Department.
DATES:
Membership is effective on the date of this notice.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Kimberly Jackson, Office of Executive Resources, 1500 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, ATTN: 1801 L Street, 6th Floor, Washington, DC 20220. Telephone: 202-622-0774.
